ideal_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM hero_attribute JOIN hero_power ON hero_attribute.hero_id = hero_power.hero_id

title: icrl:join:publisher,superhero
user_question: How many rows are related from the join of «superhero» and «publisher»?
ideal_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM superhero JOIN publisher ON superhero.publisher_id = publisher.id

title: icrl:join:race,superhero
user_question: How many rows are related from the join of «superhero» and «race»?
ideal_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM superhero JOIN race ON superhero.race_id = race.id

title: icrl:with:alignment,superhero
user_question: How many superheroes are in good condition and what are their full names?
ideal_sql: WITH good_superheroes AS (SELECT `superhero`.`full_name` FROM `superhero` JOIN `alignment` ON `superhero`.`alignment_id` = `alignment`.`id` WHERE `alignment`.`alignment` = 'Good') SELECT COUNT(*) AS `count`, GROUP_CONCAT(`full_name` SEPARATOR ', ') AS `names` FROM good_superheroes

title: icrl:with:attribute,hero_attribute
user_question: I want to know how many superheroes have intelligence and power attributes and what are the values of these attributes?
ideal_sql: WITH hero_attributes AS (SELECT `hero_id`, `attribute_id`, `attribute_value` FROM `hero_attribute` WHERE `attribute_id` IN (SELECT `id` FROM `attribute` WHERE `attribute_name` IN ('Intelligence', 'Strength'))) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT `hero_id`) AS `hero_count`, SUM(`attribute_value`) AS `total_value` FROM hero_attributes

title: icrl:with:gender,superhero
user_question: How many male superheroes are there and what are their names?
ideal_sql: WITH male_superheroes AS (SELECT `superhero`.`full_name` FROM `superhero` JOIN `gender` ON `superhero`.`gender_id` = `gender`.`id` WHERE `gender`.`gender` = 'Male') SELECT COUNT(*) AS `count`, GROUP_CONCAT(`full_name` SEPARATOR ', ') AS `names` FROM male_superheroes

title: icrl:with:hero_attribute,hero_power
user_question: Show the highest power of each attribute for heroes with high power.
ideal_sql: WITH high_power_heroes AS (SELECT `hero_power`.`hero_id` FROM `hero_power` GROUP BY `hero_power`.`hero_id` HAVING COUNT(`hero_power`.`power_id`) > 2) SELECT `hero_attribute`.`attribute_value`, COUNT(`high_power_heroes`.`hero_id`) AS hero_count FROM `hero_attribute` JOIN high_power_heroes ON `hero_attribute`.`hero_id` = `high_power_heroes`.`hero_id` GROUP BY `hero_attribute`.`attribute_value` HAVING hero_count > 1

title: icrl:with:alignment,superhero
user_question: Can I see a list of superheroes whose condition is bad and whose height is more than 180 centimeters?
ideal_sql: WITH BadSuperheroes AS (SELECT `superhero`.full_name, `superhero`.height_cm FROM `superhero` JOIN `alignment` ON `superhero`.alignment_id = `alignment`.id WHERE `alignment`.alignment = 'Bad' AND `superhero`.height_cm > 180) SELECT * FROM BadSuperheroes

title: icrl:with:alignment,superhero
user_question: How does the average height of neutral superheroes taller than 170 centimeters compare to the height of neutral superheroes shorter than 170 centimeters?
ideal_sql: WITH `neutral_superheroes_above_170` AS (SELECT AVG(`height_cm`) AS `avg_height_above_170` FROM `superhero` INNER JOIN `alignment` ON `superhero`.`alignment_id` = `alignment`.`id` WHERE `alignment`.`alignment` = 'neutral' AND `superhero`.`height_cm` > 170), `neutral_superheroes_below_170` AS (SELECT AVG(`height_cm`) AS `avg_height_below_170` FROM `superhero` INNER JOIN `alignment` ON `superhero`.`alignment_id` = `alignment`.`id` WHERE `alignment`.`alignment` = 'neutral' AND `superhero`.`height_cm` < 170) SELECT `avg_height_above_170`, `avg_height_below_170` FROM `neutral_superheroes_above_170`, `neutral_superheroes_below_170`

title: icrl:with:attribute,hero_attribute,hero_power
user_question: With an intermediate query, how many rows are there in the join of «hero_attribute» and «attribute»?
ideal_sql: WITH linked AS (SELECT 1 AS x FROM hero_attribute JOIN attribute ON hero_attribute.attribute_id = attribute.id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM linked

ideal_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM laboratory

title: icrl:having:examination
user_question: Group the number of tests based on ANA patterns and only display patterns that have between 10 and 50 tests.
ideal_sql: SELECT `ANA Pattern`, COUNT(*) AS `Number of Tests` FROM `examination` GROUP BY `ANA Pattern` HAVING `Number of Tests` BETWEEN 10 AND 50

title: icrl:having:examination
user_question: Group the average values of aCL IgG based on diagnosis and only display diagnoses that have an average greater than 0.5 and also have fewer than 50 samples for each diagnosis.
ideal_sql: SELECT `Diagnosis`, AVG(`aCL IgG`) AS `average_aCL_IgG`, COUNT(*) AS `sample_count` FROM `examination` GROUP BY `Diagnosis` HAVING `average_aCL_IgG` > 0.5 AND `sample_count` < 50

title: icrl:having:laboratory
user_question: Group the average values of GOT based on date and only display dates that have an average greater than 17 and also consider dates that have an average ALP less than 100.
ideal_sql: SELECT `Date`, AVG(`GOT`) AS `Average_GOT`, COUNT(*) AS `Record_Count` FROM `laboratory` GROUP BY `Date` HAVING AVG(`GOT`) > 17 AND COUNT(*) < 50

title: icrl:having:patient
user_question: Group the number of patients based on gender and age and only display genders that have more than 300 patients and the average age of patients in those genders is greater than 40 years.
ideal_sql: SELECT `SEX`, COUNT(*) AS `count`, AVG(TIMESTAMPDIFF(YEAR, `Birthday`, CURDATE())) AS `average_age` FROM `patient` GROUP BY `SEX` HAVING `count` > 300 AND `average_age` > 40

title: icrl:having:laboratory
user_question: Group the average values of ALP based on date and only display dates that have an average greater than 75 and also consider dates that have an average ALP less than 100.
ideal_sql: SELECT `Date`, AVG(`ALP`) as `average_ALP` FROM `laboratory` GROUP BY `Date` HAVING AVG(`ALP`) > 75 AND AVG(`ALP`) < 100

title: icrl:having:examination
user_question: Group the number of tests based on diagnosis and only display diagnoses that have more than 100 tests and also consider the number of tests for diagnoses related to the age group over 60 years.
ideal_sql: SELECT `Diagnosis`, COUNT(*) AS `Total_Examinations`, SUM(CASE WHEN `Examination Date` < DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 60 YEAR) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `Examinations_Above_60` FROM `examination` GROUP BY `Diagnosis` HAVING `Total_Examinations` > 100

title: icrl:join:examination,patient
user_question: Group the number of patients based on diagnosis and only display diagnoses that have more than 50 patients and also consider the number of patients with specific diagnoses that are between the ages of 30 and 40 years, which should be more than 20.
ideal_sql: SELECT `examination`.`Diagnosis`, COUNT(`patient`.`ID`) AS `PatientCount` FROM `examination` JOIN `patient` ON `examination`.`Diagnosis` = `patient`.`Diagnosis` GROUP BY `examination`.`Diagnosis` HAVING COUNT(`patient`.`ID`) > 50 AND SUM(CASE WHEN YEAR(CURDATE()) - YEAR(`patient`.`Birthday`) BETWEEN 30 AND 40 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 20

title: icrl:range:examination
user_question: What are the oldest and newest values of «Examination Date»?
ideal_sql: SELECT MIN(`Examination Date`) AS first_d, MAX(`Examination Date`) AS last_d FROM examination

title: icrl:range:laboratory
user_question: What are the oldest and newest values of 'Date'?
ideal_sql: SELECT MIN(Date) AS first_d, MAX(Date) AS last_d FROM laboratory

title: icrl:range:patient
user_question: What are the oldest and newest values of «First Date»?
ideal_sql: SELECT MIN(`First Date`) AS first_d, MAX(`First Date`) AS last_d FROM patient

user_question: What is the total number of bonds in the bond table?
ideal_sql: SELECT COUNT(`bond_id`) FROM `bond`

title: icrl:filter:connected
user_question: What is the highest number of atoms with the identifier TR496_27 in the connected table?
ideal_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `connected` WHERE `atom_id2` = 'TR496_27'

user_question: How many molecules have a positive label?

title: icrl:having:atom
user_question: Please display the names of elements that have more than 10 atoms.
ideal_sql: SELECT `element`, COUNT(`atom_id`) AS `atom_count` FROM `atom` GROUP BY `element` HAVING `atom_count` > 10

title: icrl:having:bond
user_question: Group the number of bonds by bond type and display only those bond types that have more than 50 bonds. Also, calculate the number of bonds for bond types that have between 50 and 100, and compare these two groups.
ideal_sql: SELECT `bond_type`, COUNT(`bond_id`) AS `count` FROM `bond` GROUP BY `bond_type` HAVING `count` > 50 OR (`count` BETWEEN 50 AND 100)

title: icrl:join:bond,connected
user_question: Display the number of atoms connected to bonds of type '=' and also calculate the number of atoms connected to bonds of type '≠' and compare these two values.
ideal_sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN `bond`.`bond_type` = '=' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS equal_bonds, SUM(CASE WHEN `bond`.`bond_type` = '≠' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS not_equal_bonds FROM `bond` JOIN `connected` ON `connected`.`bond_id` = `bond`.`bond_id`

title: icrl:having:molecule
user_question: Group the number of molecules by label and display only those labels that have more than 100 and less than 500.
ideal_sql: SELECT `label`, COUNT(*) AS `count` FROM `molecule` GROUP BY `label` HAVING `count` > 100 AND `count` < 500

title: icrl:filter:connected
user_question: Display the number of atoms connected to atoms TR466_2 and TR496_27.
ideal_sql: SELECT `atom_id2`, COUNT(`atom_id`) AS `count` FROM `connected` WHERE `atom_id2` IN ('TR466_2', 'TR496_27') GROUP BY `atom_id2`

title: icrl:join:atom,bond
user_question: Compare the number of atoms connected to bonds of type '#' with the number of atoms connected to bonds of type '='.
ideal_sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN `bond`.`bond_type` = '#' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_hash_bonds, SUM(CASE WHEN `bond`.`bond_type` = '=' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_equal_bonds FROM `atom` JOIN `bond` ON `atom`.`molecule_id` = `bond`.`molecule_id`

title: icrl:join:atom,bond
user_question: Display the number of atoms connected to bonds of type '-'.
ideal_sql: SELECT COUNT(`atom`.`atom_id`) AS `atom_count` FROM `atom` JOIN `bond` ON `atom`.`molecule_id` = `bond`.`molecule_id` WHERE `bond`.`bond_type` = '-'

title: icrl:join:atom,molecule
user_question: Compare the number of atoms connected to molecules with label '+' with the number of atoms connected to molecules with label '-'.
ideal_sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN `molecule`.`label` = '+' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `positive_atoms`, SUM(CASE WHEN `molecule`.`label` = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `negative_atoms` FROM `atom` JOIN `molecule` ON `atom`.`molecule_id` = `molecule`.`molecule_id`

title: icrl:join:atom,connected
user_question: Display the number of atoms connected to atoms of type 'h' and 'c' that each have more than 2 connected atoms.
ideal_sql: SELECT `atom`.`element`, COUNT(`connected`.`atom_id2`) AS `connected_count` FROM `atom` JOIN `connected` ON `connected`.`atom_id` = `atom`.`atom_id` WHERE `atom`.`element` IN ('h', 'c') GROUP BY `atom`.`element` HAVING COUNT(`connected`.`atom_id2`) > 2

title: icrl:join:atom,connected
user_question: Compare the number of atoms connected to atoms of type 'o' with the number of atoms connected to atoms of type 'h'.
ideal_sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN `a`.`element` = 'o' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `count_o`, SUM(CASE WHEN `a`.`element` = 'h' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `count_h` FROM `atom` AS `a` JOIN `connected` AS `c` ON `c`.`atom_id` = `a`.`atom_id`

title: icrl:join:atom,molecule
user_question: How many rows are related to the connection between «atom» and «molecule»?
ideal_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM atom JOIN molecule ON atom.molecule_id = molecule.molecule_id

title: icrl:join:bond,connected
user_question: How many rows are related to the connection between «connected» and «bond»?
ideal_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM connected JOIN bond ON connected.bond_id = bond.bond_id

title: icrl:join:bond,molecule
user_question: How many rows are related to the connection of «bond» and «molecule»?
ideal_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM bond JOIN molecule ON bond.molecule_id = molecule.molecule_id

title: icrl:with:atom,bond
user_question: Which elements have the most types of bonds in different molecules and have a number of bonds greater than a specified value?
ideal_sql: WITH ElementBondTypeCount AS (SELECT `atom`.`element`, COUNT(DISTINCT `bond`.`bond_type`) AS bond_type_count FROM `atom` JOIN `bond` ON `atom`.`molecule_id` = `bond`.`molecule_id` GROUP BY `atom`.`element` HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT `bond`.`bond_type`) > 1) SELECT `element`, bond_type_count FROM ElementBondTypeCount WHERE bond_type_count = (SELECT MAX(bond_type_count) FROM ElementBondTypeCount)

title: icrl:with:atom,bond
user_question: Which elements exist with a specific type of bond in different molecules and have a count greater than 5?
ideal_sql: WITH ElementBondCount AS (SELECT `atom`.`element`, COUNT(`bond`.`bond_id`) AS bond_count FROM `atom` JOIN `bond` ON `atom`.`molecule_id` = `bond`.`molecule_id` GROUP BY `atom`.`element`) SELECT `element` FROM ElementBondCount WHERE bond_count > 5

title: icrl:with:atom,molecule
user_question: Which molecules have a positive label and have more than 2 hydrogen atoms?
ideal_sql: WITH hydrogen_atoms AS (SELECT `molecule_id` FROM `atom` WHERE `element` = 'H' GROUP BY `molecule_id` HAVING COUNT(*) > 2) SELECT `molecule`.`label` FROM `molecule` JOIN hydrogen_atoms ON `molecule`.`molecule_id` = hydrogen_atoms.`molecule_id`

title: icrl:with:atom,bond,connected
user_question: Which atoms are connected to other atoms and have a specific type of bond, with the number of bonds connected to each atom being greater than a specific number?
ideal_sql: WITH joined_data AS (SELECT `atom`.`atom_id`, `atom`.`element`, `bond`.`bond_type` FROM `atom` JOIN `bond` ON `atom`.`molecule_id` = `bond`.`molecule_id`) SELECT `joined_data`.`atom_id`, `joined_data`.`element`, `joined_data`.`bond_type`, COUNT(`connected`.`atom_id2`) AS `connected_count` FROM `joined_data` JOIN `connected` ON `joined_data`.`atom_id` = `connected`.`atom_id` WHERE `joined_data`.`bond_type` = '-' GROUP BY `joined_data`.`atom_id`, `joined_data`.`element`, `joined_data`.`bond_type` HAVING COUNT(`connected`.`atom_id2`) > 1

title: icrl:with:atom,connected
user_question: Which atoms are connected to other atoms in different molecules and have a specific type of bond, with the number of atoms connected to each atom being greater than 3?
ideal_sql: WITH atom_connections AS (SELECT `atom`.`atom_id`, COUNT(`connected`.`atom_id2`) AS connection_count FROM `atom` JOIN `connected` ON `connected`.`atom_id` = `atom`.`atom_id` GROUP BY `atom`.`atom_id`) SELECT `atom`.`element`, `atom_connections`.`connection_count` FROM `atom` JOIN `atom_connections` ON `atom`.`atom_id` = `atom_connections`.`atom_id` WHERE `atom_connections`.`connection_count` > 3

title: icrl:with:atom,molecule,bond
user_question: Which atoms belong to molecules that have a positive label and have more than 3 bonds?
ideal_sql: WITH molecule_bonds AS (SELECT `molecule`.`molecule_id`, COUNT(`bond`.`bond_id`) AS bond_count FROM `molecule` JOIN `bond` ON `molecule`.`molecule_id` = `bond`.`molecule_id` GROUP BY `molecule`.`molecule_id` HAVING COUNT(`bond`.`bond_id`) > 3) SELECT `atom`.`atom_id` FROM `atom` JOIN molecule_bonds ON `atom`.`molecule_id` = molecule_bonds.`molecule_id` JOIN `molecule` ON `molecule`.`molecule_id` = molecule_bonds.`molecule_id` WHERE `molecule`.`label` = '+'

title: icrl:with:bond,connected,molecule
user_question: With an intermediate query, how many rows are there for the connection of «connected» and «bond»?
ideal_sql: WITH linked AS (SELECT 1 AS x FROM connected JOIN bond ON connected.bond_id = bond.bond_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM linked
